why: zkcandy has no working JSON-RPC endpoint, so resolve_l2_code.py cannot run there. results-l2/scripts/resolve_zkcandy_explorer.py substitutes two explorer endpoints for the two RPC calls. This file records the evidence that the substitute agrees with eth_getCode.
substitute_method: explorer.zkcandy.io/api?module=contract&action=getcontractcreation -> a creation record means 'contract', an empty OK result means 'no code'

cross_validation_on_era.why_era: era has BOTH a working archive RPC and a working ZKsync-era-style explorer API, so the substitute can be scored against eth_getCode ground truth
cross_validation_on_era.sample: all 8 era contract recipients + 200 era EOA recipients (random.seed(20260826))

positive_control_on_zkcandy.why: an all-EOA sweep result is also what a broken detector returns; these are real zkcandy contracts, found independently via the explorer's own tokentx/txlist data for candidate recipients
positive_control_on_zkcandy.full_chunk_test: a chunk of exactly 10 known contracts returned all 10; a mixed chunk of 5 contracts + 5 EOAs returned exactly the 5 contracts

zkcandy.above_cap: status:1 OK with ZERO results — SILENT truncation, which is why the script hard-caps at 10 and asserts every returned address was asked for

declared_limitations: no bytecode is returned: zkcandy contributes no code_len, no codehash and therefore no bytecode families (METHOD 5)
EIP-7702 delegated-eoa cannot be detected (a delegation is code, not a creation record) — zkcandy's delegated-eoa count is unknown, not zero

a genesis-deployed contract has no creation record and reads as codeless; verified for 0x..8007, 0x..800b, 0x..800a, 0x..10002, 0x..10005. All genesis contracts sit in the reserved range that METHOD 3 flags is_system, so no user-chosen counterparty can be mis-filed by this
